newsitem.title: UK: Clerical blunder left UK banks in dark on budget.
newsitem.headline: Clerical blunder left UK banks in dark on budget.

text.p: An administrative mistake left City of London banks and institutions without copies of a crucial breakdown of British Chancellor Kenneth Clarke's 1997/98 budget.

"There just weren't enough, through some administrative error," said a spokesman for the Treasury. "Obviously we are looking into it, and are involved in discussions with the Bank (of England) to sort out how it happened."

The document, known as the Red Book, contains the government's fiscal and economic forecasts, along with breakdowns of spending plans. It is made available by the Treasury, which sends copies to the Bank of England for institutions to collect after the Chancellor's speech.

One bond analyst at a Japanese bank in London said they had failed to receive a copy, and were told the problem occurred when a clerk mistakenly put two copies each of the Redbook in envelopes for organisations at the top of the list -- leaving none left for those further down.

"We had to use the internet to get the information," the bond analyst said. "We were still at it by nine o'clock at night." The Treasury spokesman said they rushed extra computer discs containing the information over to the Bank of England to appease those organisations left without a copy.
However, the delay meant many banks were unable to start the necessary analysis of the budget's fine-print -- and several irate banks have already called the Treasury to complain.
"We've had a lot of banks calling in today," the Treasury spokesman said.
No-one at the Bank of England was available for comment.
